source.name: Cave Bear
source.section: Polar Bear and Variant: Cave Bear
source.sourceWitness: Local first-print scan, with printed folios confirmed visually. The public page viewer numbers pages one ahead of the book.
source.appearanceEvidence: The printed sidebar describes coarse dark hair. Broad shoulders and the heavy head are visible in the reused Cave Bear portrait from the AD&D Monstrous Manual bundle.
source.habitatEvidence: The sidebar specifies life underground. Caves and Underdark are editorial search tags for that environment.
source.variantDerivation: The Cave Bear sidebar adds darkvision 60 ft. to the Polar Bear on the same folio. Carry over its other statistics, including its 30-ft. swim speed.

source.name: Diseased Giant Rat
source.section: Giant Rat and Variant: Diseased Giant Rats
source.sourceWitness: Local first-print scan, with printed folios confirmed visually. The public page viewer numbers pages one ahead of the book.
source.appearanceEvidence: Matches the shared Giant Rat portrait. The diseased variant describes transmission through bites and gives no visible signs.
source.habitatEvidence: Underdark, forest, swamp, and urban are tags from the legacy Giant Rat listing. Sewers is an editorial search term. The disease sidebar does not change habitat.
printingNotes: The first print uses +3 to hit and 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing. The official 2018 errata changes those to +4 and 4 (1d4 + 2).
The two roster spellings refer to the same printed variant. Both existing scope keys carry the same rules.
The source calls for one save on the hit. It gives a maximum-HP decrease every 24 hours until cure and specifies no recurring saving throw.
source.variantDerivation: Keep the Giant Rat’s statistics and traits. Use the sidebar’s replacement Bite with the errata’s attack and damage numbers.

source.name: Warhorse (Chain Mail Barding)
source.printing: First printing, September 2014, with official errata v2.0
source.section: Appendix A, Warhorse and Variant: Warhorse Armor
source.errataEvidence: The first printing gives Hooves +4 to hit. The official errata replace it with +6 for the 2014 Monster Manual Warhorse.

derivation.notes: The base Warhorse provides hit points, speed, ability scores, CR, XP, Trampling Charge, and Hooves. The nearby sidebar supplies this variant's AC and states that barding does not change CR.

source.equipmentEvidence: The Player's Handbook gives the armor's standard Stealth disadvantage and Strength threshold where applicable, and identifies barding as armor fitted to an animal. The variant uses the printed 60-ft. speed and adds no inferred armor-proficiency penalty.
source.appearanceEvidence: Editorial description based on the approved existing neutral horse image and the printed armor type. The shared portrait depicts the animal without barding.
source.habitatEvidence: Editorial tags based on trained warhorses and places where they are ridden or housed.
